problem: "a 180° error is the farthest apart two points can be" is garbled: a student reads "180° error" as the error event itself, when the point being made is that the two BPSK symbols sit 180° apart, the largest possible separation.
fix: BPSK uses two phases 180° apart, giving 1 bit per symbol. Those two symbols are as far apart as two points on a circle can be, so noise must be large to push one symbol into the other; of ASK, FSK and PSK, BPSK gives the fewest bit errors for the same signal-to-noise ratio.

problem: Sharing one medium on different carriers is frequency-division multiplexing (FDM), not frequency reuse. Frequency reuse in standard usage means reusing the same band in different cells or beams.
fix: Many signals can share one medium by sitting on different carriers. That is frequency-division multiplexing (FDM), and 2.7 builds on it.

problem: "it survives where noise is low, as in short optical links" gives the wrong reason and understates optical links. Optical fibre uses on-off keying because the source is switched on and off (intensity modulation) and direct detection is cheap, not because only short links have low noise.
fix: ASK is fragile, but it is cheap: a light source switched fully on and off is an ASK signal, which is why on-off keying suits optical fibre links.

problem: "A QAM-16 modem on the same link" clashes with the numbers: a link only 2 kHz wide cannot carry 2400 symbols per second (Nyquist needs at least 2400 Hz). The two parts of the example contradict each other.
fix: Say "A QAM-16 modem with a symbol rate of 2400 baud; find its bit rate" and drop "on the same link", so the two parts are independent.

problem: The marks are printed twice for every question, once in the header, e.g. "Q1 (remember, 2 marks)", and again at the end, "(2 marks)".
fix: Keep the marks only in the header: "Q1 (remember, 2 marks): Define the AM modulation index and state the condition for no overmodulation."

problem: The note "carrier out" can be read as "the carrier comes out", the opposite of what the figure text says (the demodulator takes the carrier back out).
fix: Change the note to "carrier removed" or "baseband out".
